recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if CDS explicitly wants a new action-level profile override on PlanDefinition.action; that would be a new design change rather than completion of FHIR-17200.
issue_request: FHIR-17200 was a Published/Persuasive CDS change request raised for STU3 asking to support workflow conformance profiles from PlanDefinition actions, with the concrete need to associate a StructureDefinition with a step. The recorded resolution was to add an optional profile element to ActivityDefinition and PlanDefinition to allow a profile to constrain resources that can satisfy an action requirement.
initial_application: The git-svn implementation commit 3c199cb863/a9e864411d includes GF#17200 and added ActivityDefinition.profile as 0..1 canonical(StructureDefinition), with short/definition text saying it identifies the profile the target resource needs to conform to. The same change touched PlanDefinition operation plumbing, but searches did not find a durable PlanDefinition.profile source element.
additional_context: ActivityDefinition and PlanDefinition are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Current PlanDefinition.action.definition[x] can reference ActivityDefinition, and PlanDefinition's application narrative says atomic actions with an ActivityDefinition are realized by applying that ActivityDefinition before applying PlanDefinition action overrides. Later FHIR-48393 removed separate shareable/publishable profile StructureDefinitions from core but did not remove ActivityDefinition.profile and does not change this issue's mechanism.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already provides the requested conformance-profile support through ActivityDefinition.profile, reachable from PlanDefinition.action.definition[x], and adding a direct StructureDefinition target or a new PlanDefinition-level profile would be redundant or ambiguous without a new work-group design decision.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied CDS issue removed shareable/publishable profile StructureDefinitions from core, but it did not remove ActivityDefinition.profile and does not affect this audit decision.
